---
title: "Row / grid container"
format: revealjs
filters:
  - value-box
---

## Default: single row, no wrap

With no `columns` attribute, boxes lay out in a flex row rather than a grid —
one column per child, no explicit count needed.

::: {.value-box-row}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
First
:::

::: {.value-box value="2"}
Second
:::

:::

## Explicit columns: grid that wraps

Four boxes at `columns="3"` must wrap onto a second row, both kept the same
height via `grid-auto-rows:1fr`.

::: {.value-box-row columns="3"}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
One
:::

::: {.value-box value="2"}
Two
:::

::: {.value-box value="3"}
Three
:::

::: {.value-box value="4"}
Four, wraps onto row two
:::

:::

## Gap and extra-style

::: {.value-box-row gap="3rem" extra-style="border:1px dashed red;"}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
Custom gap
:::

::: {.value-box value="2"}
Custom gap
:::

:::

## Passthrough: id, extra class, data/aria/role, and an unrecognised attribute

The id, an extra class, and role/aria-label/data-id all pass through — but
`top` is outside the recognised set and is left off entirely, not renamed
into a data- attribute.

::: {#kpi-row .value-box-row .custom-hook role="group" aria-label="Key metrics" data-id="row1" top="200px"}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
Kitchen sink
:::

:::

## A literal style attribute is dropped

A literal `style` would collide with the row's own generated style, so it is
dropped (with a warning) rather than producing two style attributes on one
tag.

::: {.value-box-row style="color:red"}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
Literal style is dropped
:::

:::

## An unrecognised columns value falls back to a single row

`columns="lots"` isn't a number, so this must warn and fall back to the
default flex-row behaviour rather than emitting invalid CSS or crashing.

::: {.value-box-row columns="lots"}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
Falls back to a row
:::

::: {.value-box value="2"}
Falls back to a row
:::

:::

## min-column-width sets the reflow threshold

`min-column-width` is emitted as the `--vb-row-min-col` custom property; the
stylesheet carries the default, so an unset row emits nothing extra.

::: {.value-box-row min-column-width="16rem"}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
Custom reflow width
:::

::: {.value-box value="2"}
Custom reflow width
:::

:::

## min-column-width alongside columns

::: {.value-box-row columns="4" min-column-width="10rem"}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
Grid plus a reflow width
:::

::: {.value-box value="2"}
Grid plus a reflow width
:::

:::

## A blank min-column-width emits nothing

An explicit blank counts as unset, not a value — the row wrapper carries no
custom property for it, and no half-written declaration is left behind.

::: {.value-box-row min-column-width=""}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
Blank min-column-width
:::

:::

## responsive="false" restores the rigid single row

::: {.value-box-row responsive="false"}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
Never wraps
:::

::: {.value-box value="2"}
Never wraps
:::

:::

## responsive="false" alongside columns pins the grid to exactly N

::: {.value-box-row columns="3" responsive="false"}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
Always three columns
:::

::: {.value-box value="2"}
Always three columns
:::

:::

## An unrecognised responsive value warns and keeps the default

`responsive="maybe"` is neither `true` nor `false`, so this must warn and leave
the responsive default on (no `vb-row-fixed` class) rather than crashing.

::: {.value-box-row responsive="maybe"}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
Still responsive
:::

:::

## Row-level defaults inherited by children

`icon-position`, `color`, `icon-size` and `align` are set once on the row;
neither child sets any of them, so both inherit all four.

::: {.value-box-row icon-position="left" color="bg-teal" icon-size="4em" align="right"}

::: {.value-box icon="bi-star" value="1"}
Inherits row defaults
:::

::: {.value-box icon="bi-star" value="2"}
Also inherits row defaults
:::

:::

## A child overriding one inherited attribute keeps the rest

::: {.value-box-row icon-position="right" color="bg-teal" icon-size="2rem" align="center"}

::: {.value-box icon="bi-star" value="1" color="bg-red"}
Overrides colour, keeps the other inherited defaults
:::

::: {.value-box icon="bi-star" value="2"}
Still inherits colour from the row
:::

:::

## A blank child override is not replaced by the row default

The row sets `icon-color`; a child that explicitly blanks its own
`icon-color` must keep no colour declaration at all, not fall back to the
row's value — an explicit blank is a deliberate override, same as it is
when set directly on a box.

::: {.value-box-row icon-color="red"}

::: {.value-box icon="bi-star" value="1" icon-color=""}
Blanks icon-color
:::

::: {.value-box icon="bi-star" value="2"}
Inherits icon-color from the row
:::

:::

## A non-inheritable attribute on the row never reaches children

`href` is not in the inheritable list — a row that (harmlessly) carries one
has no effect on its children, which still render as plain divs, not links.

::: {.value-box-row href="https://example.com/row"}

::: {.value-box value="1"}
Still a div, not a link
:::

:::

## An extra-style hook inherits, and a child's own value overrides it

::: {.value-box-row icon-extra-style="opacity:0.5;"}

::: {.value-box icon="bi-star" value="1"}
Inherits icon-extra-style
:::

::: {.value-box icon="bi-star" value="2" icon-extra-style="opacity:0.9;"}
Overrides icon-extra-style
:::

:::

## Inherited font-color flows through the existing value/title colour fallback

The row sets only `font-color`; the child sets none of `font-color`,
`value-color` or `title-color`, so both fall back through to the inherited
`font-color` exactly as they would to one set directly on the box.

::: {.value-box-row font-color="black"}

::: {.value-box value="7" title="Composed"}
Both value and title pick up the inherited font-color
:::

:::
